name: Inside a Holographic Superconductor
description: The inside of a planar charged black hole of anti-de Sitter space that has grown charged scalar hair below a critical temperature, the gravitational dual of a superconductor. It has no inner horizon: the Einstein-Rosen bridge collapses, the scalar field oscillates, and the spacetime ends at a spacelike Kasner singularity, sometimes after one or more Kasner inversions.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$. No component assumes a field equation.

coordinates.name: Planar

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$
Blackening function, a pure number, with $f \to 1$ at the boundary; it vanishes on the event horizon and is negative inside it
Function in the lapse, a pure number, with $\chi \to 0$ at the boundary

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, z, x, y)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $z$, $x$, and $y$ lengths, and inside the event horizon, where $f < 0$, $z$ is the time. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Final Kasner epoch

parameters.description: Kasner exponent along $t$, with $-1/3 \le p_t \le 1$; the exponent along $x$ and $y$ is $(1 - p_t)/2$, and the scalar field is $\varphi = -p_\varphi\ln\tau$ with $p_\varphi^2 = (1 - p_t)(1 + 3p_t)/2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\tau, t, x, y)$, with $\tau$ the proper time left before the singularity and $t$ both carrying dimensions of time, and $x$ and $y$ lengths, and evaluate the powers of $\tau$ with $\tau$ in a fixed unit of time. We take components in the chart $x^0 = c\tau$, $x^1 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Kasner inversion

parameters.description: Pure number with $0 < \beta \le 1$, which sets the Kasner exponent along $t$: $-\beta/(2 + \beta)$ where $\rho \gg 1$ and $\beta/(2 - \beta)$ where $\rho \ll 1$
A length, which sets the proper time the inversion takes

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\rho, t, x, y)$, with $\rho$ a pure number that falls toward the singularity at $\rho = 0$, $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and $x$ and $y$ lengths. We take components in the chart $x^1 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
